sentences.text: 4. As regards, the respondent No. 1 and respondent No 8 the learned counsel for the petitioners are directed to effect service upon the Mr. R.K.D. Choudhury, Deputy Solicitor General of India and upon Mr. B. Choudhury who is the standing counsel for the PWD.
5. The case of the petitioner herein is that the petitioner owns a plot of land measuring 3 Bigha, 17 Katha in 2 nd RS Patta No. 5, Dag No. 9 and 10.
In the said land the petitioner have erected 3 Nos. of RCC buildings which is being used as Showroom,Workshop,Washing Shed.

6. It is an admitted fact that the respondents have acquired the land ad measuring 0.0376 and 0.0541 hectares belonging to the petitioners under Dag No. 10, 2nd RS Patta No. 5 under the provisions of National Highways Act, 1956 (for short "the Act of 1956").
7.

It is also relevant to take note of that in terms of Section 3D(2) of the National Highways Act, 1956 upon issuance of the notification under Section 3D of the Act of 1956 the land vests absolutely upon the Central Government free from any encumbrances.

8. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that in view of the acquisitions so made the building which stands over the land would be effected and it would cause great inconvenience to the petitioners if immediately the petitioners are removed.
He further submitted that the petitioners have not been adequately compensated.
Page No.# 4/4 9.

Mr. C. Baruah, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the NHIDCL submitted that as the land vests upon the Central Government by virtue of Section 3E of the Act of 1956, the Competent Authority can very well take over the possession as it is statutorily mandated.

10. As regards the question of compensation the learned counsel submitted that if the petitioners are aggrieved with the amount of compensation, the petitioners can very well approach either the competent authority if the compensation has not been finalized in terms with Section 3G(5) of the Act of 1956 or seek a reference to the Arbitration as regard the inadequacy of compensation.
He however, submits that he would like to take instructions in that regard.
11. Taking into account the above let the respondents obtain instructions in that regard and place it before this Court on the next date fixed.

12. This Court however would observe that although the respondent authorities can very well take over the possession in terms with Section 3E of the Act of 1956, the Respondent Authorities may provide some reasonable time to the petitioners to shift from the present localities.
The reasonable time so mentioned would depend upon the exigency of the Respondent Authorities.
